classification_signals: The document is an edited book, with the first chapter serving as an introduction and narrative review of the field.
The chapter 'Maritime Psychology: Definition, Scope and Conceptualization' (p. 14) defines the field, outlines its scope, and previews the content of the subsequent chapters.
It synthesizes existing knowledge and identifies future research directions, characteristic of a narrative review and conceptual framework.

Subsequent chapters (e.g., 'Positive Psychology and Well-Being at Sea', 'Occupational Stress in Seafaring', 'Motion Sickness Susceptibility and Management at Sea') contain case studies, empirical findings, and further reviews, which are synthesized by the introductory chapter's scope.
title: Maritime Psychology: Research in Organizational & Health Behavior at Sea

environmental_features: prolonged separation from family and social networks

theory_commitments.specific_claim: Job demands (e.g., workload, emotional demands) and job resources (e.g., social support, autonomy) interact to predict employee well-being and organizational outcomes, which is applicable to the maritime context.

Individuals strive to obtain, retain, and protect resources (e.g., energy, social support, self-esteem), and stress occurs when resources are threatened, lost, or when investment of resources does not yield expected gains, a common experience in maritime work.

mechanism_chain.description: Psychosocial factors in the maritime environment lead to stress and burnout, which in turn affect seafarers' health behavior and overall well-being.

steps.from_construct: high job demands (e.g., long hours, responsibility)
lack of social support and isolation
steps.to_construct: feelings of loneliness and reduced coping capacity

steps.from_construct: psychological strain and reduced coping capacity
steps.to_construct: negative health behaviors (e.g., poor diet, substance use) and decreased well-being
